Let the two parts of \(K_{6,6}\) be \(A=\{a_1,\dots,a_6\}\) and \(B=\{b_1,\dots,b_6\}\). Encode an orientation by a \(6\times 6\) binary matrix \(M\), where
\[
M_{ij}=1 \iff a_i\to b_j.
\]
Eulerian means every vertex has indegree \(3\) and outdegree \(3\), so \(M\) has every row sum and every column sum equal to \(3\).

The automorphism group is
\[
\operatorname{Aut}(K_{6,6})\cong (S_6\times S_6)\rtimes C_2,
\]
where \(S_6\times S_6\) permutes rows and columns, and the part-swap sends
\[
M\mapsto J-M^T.
\]

Thus we classify \(6\times 6\) \(0\)-\(1\) matrices with all row and column sums \(3\), under row/column permutations and complement-transpose.

A finite classification under row/column permutations gives the following seven representatives, written as the six row-supports:

\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c|c}
\text{class} & \text{row supports} & |\operatorname{Stab}_{S_6\times S_6}| & \text{orbit size} \\
\hline
A & 123,123,123,456,456,456 & 2592 & 200\\
B & 123,123,124,356,456,456 & 32 & 16200\\
C & 123,123,145,246,356,456 & 12 & 43200\\
D & 123,124,125,346,356,456 & 12 & 43200\\
E & 123,124,135,246,356,456 & 12 & 43200\\
F & 123,124,135,256,346,456 & 4 & 129600\\
G & 123,124,156,256,345,346 & 24 & 21600
\end{array}
\]

These seven exhaust all row/column classes: their row/column orbit sizes sum to
\[
200+16200+43200+43200+43200+129600+21600=297200,
\]
which is the coefficient
\[
[x_1^3\cdots x_6^3](e_3(x_1,\dots,x_6))^6,
\]
the total number of ordered row-labeled matrices with row and column sums \(3\).

Now apply the extra part-swap \(M\mapsto J-M^T\). It fixes the row/column classes
\[
A,B,E,F,G
\]
and swaps the two classes
\[
C\leftrightarrow D.
\]
So the extended orbits have sizes
\[
200,\quad 16200,\quad 43200,\quad 129600,\quad 21600,\quad 43200+43200=86400.
\]

Listed in increasing order, the multiset of orbit sizes is

\[
\boxed{\{200,\,16200,\,21600,\,43200,\,86400,\,129600\}}.
\]
